'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***Ten [[mine clearer]]s are killed and 12 others are injured while working at a [[Halo Trust]] compound in [[Baghlan Province|Baghlan]]. Afghan officials blamed the [[Taliban]] for the attack while the [[ISIL]] claimed responsibility for it. The Taliban denied responsibility for the attack and Halo Trust reports that local Taliban militants arrived at the scene of the attack defending the miners and shooting the attackers. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-57410265 (BBC News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The [[Economist Intelligence Unit]] releases its annual [[Global Liveability Ranking]] assessment, ranking the world's [[most livable cities]]. [[Auckland]], [[New Zealand]] replaces long-time first place holder [[Vienna]], [[Austria]], largely because of New Zealand's handling of the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand|COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/auckland-ranked-most-liveable-city-in-the-world/ar-AAKRB9q?ocid=uxbndlbing (MSN)]

'''Business and economy'''
*North American [[energy company]] [[TC Energy]] terminates its [[Keystone Pipeline]] project, which many environmentalists and [[Indigenous peoples of the Americas|Native Americans]] have opposed, citing the risk of pollution and potential damage to wildlife. The move comes nearly five months after [[President of the United States|United States President]] [[Joe Biden]] signed an [[Executive Order 13990|executive order]] to revoke the permit that was granted to the company for the construction of the project's fourth phase. [https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/energy-commodities/canadian-company-tc-energy-drops-keystone-pipeline-project (''Business Times'')]
*[[El Salvador]] becomes the first country to accept [[Bitcoin]] as legal tender, after the [[Legislative Assembly of El Salvador|Legislative Assembly]] votes 62–22 to pass a bill submitted by [[President of El Salvador|President]] [[Nayib Bukele]] classifying the cryptocurrency as such. [https://en.mercopress.com/2021/06/10/bitcoin-legal-tender-in-el-salvador-first-country-ever (MercoPress)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Gwangju building collapse]]
**Nine people are killed and eight more injured as a five-storey building being demolished in [[Gwangju, South Korea]], collapses onto a bus. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/9-dead-building-collapses-south-korea-bury-bus-14979730 (CNA)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reopens indoor dining for bars and restaurants as well as gyms as the number of [[COVID-19]] cases continues to decline and the number of [[COVID-19 vaccination in France|vaccinations]] increases. Rules for travellers from within the [[European Union]] are also eased, while cultural venues can relax their measures. The curfew has also been changed to 11:00 p.m. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/france-enjoys-indoor-dining-with-new-lifting-of-covid-19-curbs (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Macedonia]]
****[[North Macedonia]] receives 30,000 doses of [[Sinovac Biotech|Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] donated by [[Turkey]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/north-macedonia-receives-30-000-vaccine-doses-donated-by-turkey/2268553 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] delays its easing of the COVID-19-related [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in [[Lisbon]], [[Braga]], [[Vale de Cambra]] and [[Odemira]] until June 27 amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/covid-resurgence-slows-lifting-of-lisbon-lockdown-01623254113 (''Barron's'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 7,540 new cases in the past 24 hours, the highest single-day total since February 26 amid an increase in the number of [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]] cases. [https://www.itv.com/news/2021-06-09/covid-7540-new-cases-reported-in-biggest-daily-increase-since-end-of-february (''ITV News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington (state)]]
****[[Seattle]] becomes the first major U.S. city to fully vaccinate 70% of residents 12 and older. [https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/health/durkan-seattle-becomes-first-major-city-to-fully-vaccinate-70-of-residents/?amp=1 (''The Seattle Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
***The number of [[COVID-19 vaccine]] doses administered in [[Pakistan]] surpasses 10 million. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1873391/world (''Arab News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Peru]]
***[[Peru]] reports its first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]], which was originally detected in [[India]] in the southern city of [[Arequipa]]. [https://riotimesonline.com/brazil-news/miscellaneous/covid-19/peru-confirms-its-first-case-of-the-indian-variant-of-the-coronavirus/ (''The Rio Times'')]
*The World Mosquito Programme  reports that an experiment in which [[mosquito]]es purposefully infected with ''[[Wolbachia]]'' bacteria were released in [[Yogyakarta]], [[Indonesia]] saw rates of [[dengue fever]] cases in the city drop by 77%, and an 86% reduction in related hospitalizations. [https://www.bbc.com/news/health-57417219 (BBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*A court in [[Russia]] begins the process of evaluation of a request to label opposition activist [[Alexei Navalny]]'s network [[Anti-Corruption Foundation]] as "extremists", which, according to Navalny's lawyers and allies, would prevent them from running for office and carrying out their activities. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-court-weighs-pre-election-knockout-blow-kremlin-critic-navalnys-network-2021-06-09/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Mongolian presidential election]]
**Mongolians head to the polls to elect a new [[President of Mongolia|president]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/9/mongolia-votes-for-new-president-amid-covid-outbreak (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[Supreme Court of Vanuatu]] Justice Oliver Saksak places a stay on speaker [[Gracia Shadrack]]'s vacation of 18 seats of parliament until a court can formally consider the dispute. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/444381/judge-stays-vanuatu-speaker-s-move (RNZ International)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Vietnam]] announces that it plans to postpone the [[2021 Southeast Asian Games|Southeast Asia Games]], one of the five subregional Games of the [[Olympic Council of Asia]], until next year, citing concerns over the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. Eight of the 11 member states of the Southeast Asian Games Federation have objected to Vietnam's proposal to postpone the competition, according to a statement from the Olympic Council of Malaysia. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/sport/vietnam-postpone-sea-games-covid-19-meeting-oppose-14980660 (CNA)]
